_INSTRUCCIONES:
Highlights & Lowlights por mes, transcritos de las slides 'EVF - Highlights & Lowlights' del VEMO Monthly Financial Review. Para agregar un mes nuevo copia un bloque y cambia la llave (ej. 'Jul-26'). El campo body acepta HTML: usa '• ' y '
• ' para los sub-bullets. Los montos ($X.Xm), porcentajes y bps se colorean automaticamente. Opcional: pnl_revenue / pnl_gp / pnl_ebitda / pnl_ni con {'bud': '...', 'mom': '...'} para sobrescribir el P&L Commentary automatico.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body:
• Record consumption of MXN$ 786k for Watts B2B, driven primarily by LAFA reaching MXN$ 722k (+17.5% MoM).
• Corporate EV customers continue to show commercial traction in both VEMO's public charging network and Watts B2B, with 4 new customers signed: Rotoplas, Newell, Driver and YesPablo (renting for ride-hailing users).

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit programs
highlights.body: • No additional chargers were signed during the month; however, progress was made integrating previously executed agreements into the Watts platform.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 11.5m, with: (i) MXN $5.7m comes from the EPC being developed for the ChaaS project for Holcim; (ii) MXN$ 2.9m from EPC projects for KIA (MXN $1.8m for chargers for their assembly plant), and other projects for Sigma, KOF, GNP and Difarmer; and (iii) MXN$ 2.1m comes from OEMs such as BYD, Stellantis and KIA dealerships.
• Total Pipeline of MXN$ 80.0m, with: (i) MXN$ 52.0m comes from OEMs, such as BYD, GM, Toyota, BMW, Changan, Hyundai, JAC, Nissan and Stellantis; and (ii) MXN$ 28.0m from corporate customers (such as Coppel, Phillip Morris, Packmail, Sigma, and Difarmer).

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body: • Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $3.0m (-16.8% vs. Budget), out of which: (i) MXN $1.7m came from the construction of a public charging site with a BYD dealership; (ii) MXN $0.7m came from Stellantis and Toyota dealerships; and (iii) MXN $0.6m from corporate EPC projects came, exclusively from Sigma.

lowlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
lowlights.body: • We continue facing delays in the implementation of the C40 project as well as other EPC opportunities due to organizational changes at Bimbo and adjustments to the scope of its EV initiatives.

lowlights.title: EMSP
lowlights.body: • Slow progress on the BMW co-branding project.

lowlights.title: ZEE
lowlights.body: • Sigma contract has not yet been signed, still under review by Sigma team.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body: • Record consumption of MXN $797k (+39.9% MoM) for Watts B2B, driven by increases across most customers. The main three clients being LAFA (ride hailing), Adet (last mile delivery), and ConectaBee (electrical devices installation company, including residential EV chargers).

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit programs
highlights.body:
• Reached a total of 18 DC chargers and 1.685 MW of installed capacity.
• Signed 2 additional 60kW chargers in Monterrey with the Cleber dealership group.
• Signed and onboarded in Watts the first 60kW charger in Tijuana with a BYD dealership, enabling the launch of VEMO LTO in the city during March.
• Activated a 150 kW CCS1 charger in Morelia.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 7.0m, with MXN $5.3m expected to be executed in March and the remaining MXN $1.7m in April. Specifically: (i) MXN $5.7m from the EPC projects under development for ChaaS (Holcim); (ii) MXN$ 0.8m from OEMs (e.g., BYD dealerships); and (iii) MXN$ 0.3m from EPC projects for Sigma, KOF (Coca Cola FEMSA), and Stellantis.
• Total pipeline of MXN$ 124.0m, most relevant including: (i) MXN $21.1m from BYD charger purchases; (ii) MXN $19.7m from GM dealership EPC projects; (iii) MXN $10.0m from Coppel corporate EPC projects and other clients such as Holcim, Nadro, Difarmer, and Packmail; (iv) MXN $6.0m from KIA assembly plants, and additional OEM related projects (Hyundai, Nissan, Changan, Toyota, JAC, BMW); and (v) MXN $67.2m from other small companies and projects.
• Of note, we have been invited in March to bid on a $130m project with DHL that involves EPC for 20 different sites during 2026. We have a strong history working with DHL over the past years and believe there is a decent likelihood of being awarded a portion of the sites.

highlights.title: MELI
highlights.body: • We are currently in negotiations with MELI to become the enabler of the whole EV ecosystem for MELI and its carriers, including FAAS, CHAAS, EPC, ZEE and/or Watts B2B. Very fluid dialogue with C-level.

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body:
• Completed the installation of 27 additional vehicles for LALA, reaching a total fleet of 259 vehicles, becoming our largest external client and promoter.
• Contract with Sigma has been signed after months of negotiation, for the telemetry of 62 vehicles and 50 chargers.

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body:
• Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $4.5m (-46.4% vs. Budget), of which: (i) MXN $1.9m came from EPC projects at the KIA assembly plant; (ii) MXN $1.7m from subsequent construction phases of a public charging site with a BYD dealership; (iii) MXN $0.4m from a corporate EPC project for Sigma; and (iv) MXN $0.5m from other small projects.
• Slow start to the year with limited backlog conversion during January-February; however, stronger pipeline activity is expected to drive higher conversion levels in Q2.

lowlights.title: EPC
lowlights.body:
• Key projects with GM dealerships (MXN $1.2m), Porsche (MXN $1.1m), and Heineken (MXN $0.9m) were not secured. In the case of Porsche's project, they decided not pursue the project. In the case of Heineken, Enel was awarded the deal.
• Security-related disruptions in Mexico impacted customs operations, delaying charger imports and shifting execution of Sigma and KIA projects into March.

lowlights.title: EMSP
lowlights.body: • Slow progress in Guadalajara's EMSP, due to a low number of DC chargers installed by dealerships.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body:
• Record consumption of MXN $1.0m (+25.5% MoM), driven primarily by LAFA (MXN $954k) our most relevant Watts B2B client. Ongoing discussions to cover most of their charging needs (ca. 300 units currently, targeting 500 units by YE).
• Signed Watts B2B contract with Rotoplas (water storage company) for 10 vehicles.

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit program
highlights.body:
• BYD Iztapalapa public charging site reached COD and is active in Watts with 6 120kW chargers (12 connectors), under an EPC + EMSP structure we aim to replicate in non-LTO cities.
• Signed EMSP with a Buick GMC Cadillac dealership (Andrade's group) (1 CCS1 60 kW + 1 CCS1 150 kW) in Mexico City.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 38.0m, with MXN $5.4m expected to be executed in April. Mainly including: (i) MXN $23.0m from DHL project (300 AC chargers and EPC of 4 sites, execution expected June-July); (ii) MXN$ 2.2m from Coppel; (iii) MXN$ 1.5m from 1 new site for the Holcim's CHAAS project; (iv) MXN $0.6m from KIA's assembly plant; and (v) MXN $1.1m from various other small projects including BYD's dealerships.
• Total pipeline of MXN$ 210.0m, most relevant including: (i) MXN $25m from public charging infrastructure for Andrade's group (18 different dealerships, potential CHAAS + EMSP); (ii) MXN $22.3m from GM and MG dealership's EPC projects (100 and 150kW DC chargers, potential EMSP); (iii) MXN $8.5m from el Globo; (iv) MXN $8.0m from Coppel corporate sites; (v) MXN $7.0m for BYD dealerships and several other projects from corporate customers and dealerships that may include EMSP in other cities such as Guadalajara.
• Of note, the original full scope of the DHL project was 20 sites and MXN $130m. However, went ahead with 17 sites and an estimated Capex of MXN $90m. Out of this, VEMO was awarded with the charger's supply for the full scope and the EPC of 4 sites. On the other hand, 10 sites were awarded to C-NEUTRAL, 2 sites to Latnnova and 1 we still do not have the intel.

highlights.title: MELI
highlights.body: • Ongoing discussions to support their EV initiatives leveraging strong relationship with senior mgmt. Initial projects to include a pilot test of ZEE for ca. 10 units and charging infrastructure evaluation on one of their largest sites in Monterrey.

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body:
• Signed Sigma's contract (61 vehicles, 50 chargers), with telemetry installation expected in April.
• We currently have a total of 456 vehicles from external customers (383 contracted / 73 pilots), with key clients including LALA (262), Maxus (30), and Grupo Modelo (21).

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body:
• Total EPC revenues closed at MXN$ 8.4m (-2.0% vs. Budget), of which: (i) MXN $4.2m came from the execution of 2 sites part of the Holcim CHAAS project; (ii) MXN $2.8m from EPC projects at the KIA assembly plant; (iii) MXN $0.9m from the last phases of construction of a public charging site with a BYD dealership; and (iv) MXN $0.5m from a corporate EPC project for Sigma and GNP.
• EPC projects recognized for Q1 reached MXN $15.7m, MXN $4.8m below budget. Further, we faced a slow start of the year, with limited projects converted to backlog (especially during Jan-Feb). On the other hand, pipeline activity has increased, resulting in the expectation of growing conversion into backlog of several opportunities during Q2.

lowlights.title: Watts B2B
lowlights.body: • Delays in the signature of Watts B2B accounts for UMD and YesPablo, two ride-hailing companies that are electrifying their fleets, and currently have ca. 140 and 10 EVs, respectively.

lowlights.title: EMSP
lowlights.body: • Projects in Guadalajara with 3 different dealership groups are part of the pipeline as EPC + EMSP and under negotiation, however, none of them are expected to yield revenues in H1.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body:
• Watts B2B consumption reached MXN $1.0m, driven primarily by LAFA (MXN $958k), our most relevant Watts B2B client. We are working on a broader integration with LAFA, including a guaranteed 17.5% discount and the implementation of DiDi discount as well as additional corporate customers available at Petrarca hub, which is expected to reinforce VEMO as LAFA's preferred charging network.
• The UMD contract was signed in May (independent mobility platform serving the Jewish community; 200-vehicle fleet, 70 EVs).

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit program
highlights.body:
• KIA's co-branding project generated MXN $2.7m during the month. BMW co-branding project has been completed, but traction and conversion remained limited, resulting in a final project value of MXN $400k.
• Continued negotiations with Guadalajara dealerships for EPC/CHAAS + EMSP projects; discussions with a new group GP Auto that is interested in EMSP (30 dealerships).

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 40.0m, with MXN $9.9m expected to be executed in May. Mainly including: (i) MXN $23.0m from DHL project (300 AC chargers and EPC of 4 sites, execution expected June-July); (ii) MXN$ 6.6m from Coppel; (iii) MXN$ 4.4m from the first two sites of the ChaaS project for Andrade's group dealership, corresponding to the public charging infrastructure for 2 GM dealerships; (iv) MXN $2.4m from KIA's assembly plant; (v) MXN $1.5m for the remaining Holcim ChaaS sites; (vi) MXN $1.0m for dealership group FAME and other smaller projects.
• Total pipeline of MXN $75.7m, most relevant including: (i) MXN $36.0m from public charging infrastructure for Andrade's group (18 different dealerships, potential CHAAS + EMSP), execution expected in H2'26; (ii) MXN $15.0m from GM and MG dealerships EPC projects; (iii) MXN $8.2m from EPC projects for Monterrey ride-hailing company Casco Dharma; (iv) MXN $6.0m from Guadalajara dealership group MAG; (v) MXN $5.5m from DHL; and (vi) MXN $5.0m from dealership group FAME BYD.

highlights.title: MELI
highlights.body: • Discussions with Mercado Libre remain at an early stage and include 2 potential avenues: (i) FaaS for EVs, subject to positive TCO case, although current daily driving distances make the EV business case challenging; (ii) potential charging infrastructure and/or software opportunities to support Mercado Libre's broader fleet electrification strategy.

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body: • With the installation of Sigma's vehicles, we currently have a total of 500 vehicles from external customers (435 contracted / 65 pilots), with key clients including LALA (262), Sigma (50), Maxus (30), and Grupo Modelo (21).

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body: • Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $1.1m (-87.3% vs. Budget), of which: (i) MXN $0.5m came from an EPC project from Amports; (ii) MXN $0.3m from Sigma; and (iii) MXN $0.3m from other smaller projects. The decrease was driven primarily by charger arrivals close to month-end, together with changes to the inventory and delivery process, which prevented chargers from being delivered to customers on time for April revenue recognition. Even though sales have been consolidated and backlog has grown through the DHL and Andrade projects, execution is expected to be delayed toward H2'26, as these projects depend either on charger availability or progress with CFE.

lowlights.title: EMSP
lowlights.body: • No additional charger has been signed during April.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body: • Two new contracts have been signed: BYD trucks (for their testing vehicles) and UMD (independent mobility platform serving the Jewish community; 200-vehicle fleet, 70 EVs).

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit program
highlights.body:
• Signed a 180kW CCS1 charger at a GM dealership in Mazatlan.
• Ford issued a new order for VEMO Credit program for MXN $670k.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 45.0m, with MXN $6.2m expected to be executed in June. Mainly including: (i) MXN $23.0m from DHL project; (ii) MXN$ 14.0m from the additional sites of the ChaaS project for Andrade's group dealership, corresponding to the public charging infrastructure for 2 GM dealerships; (iii) MXN$ 4.4m from Coppel; (iv) MXN $1.5m for the remaining Holcim ChaaS sites; (v) MXN $1.3m from KIA's assembly plant; (vi) MXN $2.8m from other smaller projects.
• Total pipeline of MXN $121m, most relevant including: (i) ~MXN$40m on a very early stage — we've been invited to participate on a tender for LALA that considers the EPC for 32 sites installing DC chargers from 30, 44 and 60kW; (ii) MXN $26.0m from public charging infrastructure for Andrade's group (18 different dealerships, potential CHAAS + EMSP), execution expected in H2'26; (iii) MXN $11m and a second tender for GM assembly plants for EPC and OEM; (iv) MXN $8.2m from EPC projects for Monterrey ride-hailing company Casco Dharma; (v) MXN $6.0m from Guadalajara dealership group MAG; and (vi) several projects around MXN $4-5m for dealership groups such as Ismo, Dalton, Grupo Mena, etc.

highlights.title: MELI
highlights.body: • Discussions with Mercado Libre are being funneled to the repair of their existing infrastructure either as EPC or ChaaS (at a very early stage on the negotiation process) and the installation of telemetry in their existing vehicles (pilot test units will be installed in June).

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body:
• With the installation of Sigma's and Hutchinson port's vehicles, we currently have a total of 531 vehicles from external customers (456 contracted / 75 pilots), with key clients including LALA (262), Sigma (57), Maxus (30), and Grupo Modelo (21).
• Advanced discussions with Andesmar to implement ZEE in 17 units in Buenos Aires. This would represent ZEE's first international customer and a strategic milestone in the platform's regional expansion.

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body: • Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $6.4m (-29.5% vs. Budget), of which: (i) MXN $1.8m came from an EPC and chargers for KIA assembly plants; (ii) MXN $1.7m from Coppel; (iii) MXN $1.0m from dealership group Fame; and (iv) MXN $1.9m from other smaller projects.

lowlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
lowlights.body: • Watts B2B consumption reached MXN $852k (-14.8% MoM), driven by a 12% decline from LAFA, our largest customer, following the launch of their own charging hub as well as operational issues related to employee turnover. In response, we have developed a revised proposal centered around the utilization of our Gran Oso hub, offering a more attractive operational solution for LAFA.

lowlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
lowlights.body: • Delays on the signature of Andrade's projects and DHL contracts have prevented more pipeline to become backlog; long lead times for the execution of projects that require CFE (Andrade) and lack of availability of Charger for DHL push the projects to H2.

lowlights.title: EMSP
lowlights.body: • Delays in signature from grupo FAME (8 chargers, 60kW GBT).

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body: • Watts B2B revenues reached MXN$ 908k (+6.6% MoM). The increase was mainly driven by LAFA's consumption, which reached 123,029 kWh (+17% MoM), its highest consumption to date. The second largest customer increase was Conectabee, which returned to April consumption levels, followed by Heineken. LAFA's increased usage was driven by the incorporation of additional fleet. BYD Trucks and ride-hailing company UMD, both recently signed, have begun using our network.

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit program
highlights.body:
• 11 new chargers signed, which are expected to improve VCN's footprint by adding GBT 60 kW DC chargers across 9 cities (Celaya, Hermosillo, Querétaro, Lázaro Cárdenas, Morelia, Uruapan, Veracruz, Xalapa and Zamora), as well as a 120 kW CCS1 charger in Mazatlán.
• The BYD Iztapalapa charging site was officially inaugurated during a high-visibility event attended by BYD, fleet operators, and prospective customers. We believe the site can serve as a flagship EMSP reference case for other dealership groups, particularly in cities where we still lack fast-charging infrastructure.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 56.7m, with MXN $10m expected to be executed in July. Mainly including: (i) MXN$ 25.0m from the ChaaS project for Grupo Andrade, which includes EMSP and is expected to expand VCN's footprint through 7 sites with DC chargers ranging from 60 kW to 150 kW; (ii) MXN$ 21.0m from the DHL project, covering the supply of 300 AC chargers and the EPC work at 4 sites; (iii) MXN$ 4.3m from corporate EPC for 1 Coppel site that is almost completed; (iv) MXN$ 1.6m for dealership group FAME; (v) MXN$ 1.6m from KIA's assembly plant; (vi) MXN$ 1.5m from the remaining Holcim ChaaS sites; and (vii) MXN$ 1.5m from other smaller projects.
• Total pipeline of MXN $105.8m, most relevant including: (i) MXN$ 19m from remaining Grupo Andrade ChaaS + EMSP; (ii) MXN$ 12.6m from GM dealership projects; (iii) MXN$ 11m from a corporate GM project to provide chargers and O&M for assembly plants and MXN$ 1.6m from additional dealership EPC; (iv) MXN$ 8.2m from EPC projects for Monterrey-based ride-hailing company Casco Dharma; (v) MXN$ 6.0m from Guadalajara dealership group MAG; and (vi) several MXN$ 3-5m EPC opportunities with dealership groups, with the remaining pipeline distributed across additional small and mid-sized dealership/corporate EPC opportunities.

highlights.title: MELI
highlights.body: • MELI is currently prioritizing expense reduction, which has slowed EV-related projects. ZEE telemetry and intelligent chargers are being tested as potential levers to improve current fleet utilization and reduce operating costs. Next month, discussions are expected to focus on positioning VEMO as the charging infrastructure ecosystem for Mercado Libre's carriers.

highlights.title: PEMEX
highlights.body: • Continues to show interest in developing public charging infrastructure and has indicated a preference for a larger-scale project, rather than limiting the initial scope to two sites.

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body:
• Monthly contracted ZEE vehicles increased from 456 to 466 (+2.2% MoM, +7.9% vs budget), adding 2 vehicles for Sigma, 4 vehicles for LALA and 4 vehicles for commercial vans OEM Upower (Vizeon). Pilot tests have started with Oxxo and Mercado Libre.
• The Buenos Aires's project with Andesmar remains in progress, focused on the homologation process required to install the telemetry in the vehicles.

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body: • Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $2.1m (-77.4% vs. Budget), of which: (i) MXN $1.2m came from an EPC for Tesla; (ii) MXN $0.5m from Coppel; and (iii) MXN $0.4m from other smaller projects.

lowlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
lowlights.body: • No additional B2B customer was signed during June.

lowlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
lowlights.body: • It was not possible to recognize the execution of Coppel's due to customer-side personnel unavailability, which shifted MXN$ 4.3m from June to July. Of note, H2 execution is expected to begin catching up on YTD underperformance, supported by projects signed between April and June (mainly DHL and Grupo Andrade) which drove record backlog.

highlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
highlights.body: • Watts B2B revenues reached a record MXN$ 1.4m (+55.2% MoM). The increase was mainly driven by LAFA's consumption, which reached 185,747 kWh (+51% MoM) and MXN$ 1.3m, its highest consumption to date.

highlights.title: EMSP: Co-branding and credit program
highlights.body: • During July two previously signed chargers reached COD and became active in Watts: i) Chevrolet dealership in Oaxaca, with 1 CCS1 60 kW DC charger, and ii) BYD dealership in Xalapa, with 1 GB/T 60 kW DC charger. Including these sites, the EMSP portfolio comprises 27 DC chargers representing 3,565 kW across 20 cities.

highlights.title: EPC-Related Sales
highlights.body: • YTD EPC-related sales reached MXN$ 94m, of which MXN$ 26m corresponds to 10 ChaaS-related projects. YTD executed and recognized revenues reached MXN$ 32.5m, providing significant execution coverage for the coming months.

highlights.title: Selected Backlog & Pipeline
highlights.body:
• Total backlog of MXN$ 59.9m, with most expected to be executed in August and October.
• Total pipeline of MXN $234.0m, most relevant including: (i) MXN$ 19m from remaining Grupo Andrade ChaaS + EMSP, (ii) MXN$ 5.4m the second phase of the GM assembly-plants charging infrastructure, and (iii) MXN$ 3.8m from chargers for KIA dealerships, with the remaining pipeline distributed across additional small and mid-sized dealership/corporate EPC opportunities.

highlights.title: ZEE
highlights.body:
• Monthly contracted ZEE vehicles increased from 466 to 620 (+33.0% MoM, +24.7% vs budget), adding 154 vehicles for LALA, bringing LALA's total to 421 vehicles. Sigma Alimentos remains the second largest customer, with 59 monitored vehicles.
• LALA has indicated its intention to acquire 300 BYD vehicles, which could be instrumented with ZEE before year-end. Other material opportunities include Oxxo, with potential for 200 vehicles, while pilot tests are underway with MELI's carriers and Bimbo. A cost analysis conducted during the period supported the product's competitiveness in the market. As reminder, our strategic goal is to get into the kitchen of these large corporates through ZEE, which allows us to build relationships with their Ops teams, and increase our prospects of upselling from within.

lowlights.title: Total EPC/O&M
lowlights.body: • Total EPC revenues closed at MXN $9.5m (+3.3% vs Budget), of which: (i) MXN $3.7m came from Coppel; (ii) MXN $3.5m from DHL charger supply; (iii) MXN $1.7m from KIA; and (iv) MXN $0.6m from other smaller projects. However, reported revenue closed at MXN $2.4m after two prior-period corrections: the reclassification of three Holcim sites to ChaaS for MXN $5.6m, and the removal of MXN $1.5m in duplicated income on 2026 projects.

lowlights.title: ChaaS Offsite and Watts B2B
lowlights.body: • No additional B2B customer was signed during July.

pnl_revenue.bud: MXN -$21.5m: Driven by: (i) lower Interco EPC (-$15.6m), and (ii) lower third-party EPC (-$6.8m). July revenues reached (+$9.5m), after a clean-up of -$7.1m as part of the 2026 pre-audit clean up: (i) Holcim contract, previously booked as EPC (-$5.6m), was reclassified to ChaaS, and duplicated revenues from 2026 projects were reversed (-$1.5m). This was partially offset by higher contracted revenues (+$0.9m) mainly from ZEE services for LTO EV vehicles, now booked here as the ZEE.
pnl_revenue.mom: MXN +$0.7m: Driven by: (i) higher contracted revenues (+$0.6m) and (ii) higher third-party EPC (+$0.4m); partly offset by (iii) lower Interco EPC (-$0.2m).

pnl_gp.bud: MXN -$6.9m: Driven by lower revenues (-$21.5m), partially offset by lower EPC Direct Cost (+$14.5m). Gross Profit Margin was mainly affected by the revenue shortfall; on a normalized basis, GP Mg remains in line with historical levels (ca. 26%).
pnl_gp.mom: MXN -$1.8m: Mainly driven by revenue shortfall of -$7.1m.

pnl_ebitda.bud: MXN -$7.0m: Driven by: (i) lower GP (-$6.9m), and (ii) slightly higher SG&A (-$0.1m) on account of Q2 Insurance broker amortization (ca. -$0.4m); partially offset by (a) lower payroll (+$0.2m) and (b) lower Corp. & CF SG&A (+$0.1m).
pnl_ebitda.mom: MXN -$0.9m: Driven by: (i) a lower GP (-$1.8m), and (ii) higher CF & Corp. SG&A (-$0.2m). This was partially offset by a lower DL SG&A (+$1.1m), due to cancellation of provisions from 2025, that will no longer be executed during 2026.

pnl_ni.bud: MXN -$6.9m: Driven by a lower EBITDA (-$7.0m).
pnl_ni.mom: MXN -$0.8m: Mainly driven by lower EBITDA (-$0.9m).
